item.text: The sandbox continues to deny all local filesystem reads, so I cannot safely inspect or edit the existing notebook or manifest. I did complete a fresh web pass across all eight chapters in order, including contrary searches: technical restraint/arms-control evidence, negotiation alternatives, POW-access and Ukraine-side abuse material, official social-transfer records, household statistics, audit/budget execution, and asset/disclosure searches. Continuation research was completed across all eight chapters in order. No score or ranking was assigned.

The local notebook and `research-ledger-manifest.json` could not be read or updated because the filesystem sandbox rejected repository access. The units below are therefore provisional append-only handoff entries, beginning at `E035`; existing IDs were not renumbered.

## 1B — Nuclear policy and safeguards

**E035 — 1B.2, 1B.4, 1B.7, 1B.8**

On 20 April 2022, Russia notified the United States under New START before testing an ICBM. The U.S. Department of Defense described the test as routine and not a threat, providing contrary evidence to the more escalatory signaling record. This is a formal Russian arms-control compliance action, attributable to the Russian state and institutionally relevant to Putin’s presidential authority, but not proof of a personal order.

Locator: official U.S. Department of Defense statement, 20 April 2022, final substantive paragraph.  
Source: [Department of Defense ICBM statement](https://www.defense.gov/News/Releases/Release/Article/3005764/pentagon-press-secretary-john-f-kirby-statement-regarding-russian-icbm/).  
Period fit: direct 2022 event.  
Disposition: final evidence, high authority; contrary/restraint evidence.

**E036 — 1B.3, 1B.4, 1B.7, 1B.8**

The UNODA 2022 Yearbook records that New START remained the principal strategic-arms limitation framework, but implementation was incomplete because of disagreements over inspections. This adds an institutional arms-control finding but does not establish whether Putin personally caused the dispute or whether safeguards failed.

Locator: UNODA Yearbook 2022, Chapter 1, New START discussion.  
Source: [UNODA 2022 Yearbook](https://yearbook-archive.unoda.org/2022/chapter1.html).  
Period fit: annual 2022 review.  
Disposition: final evidence, high authority; unresolved attribution and implementation limits.

Shortfall remains: no primary 2022 Russian doctrine revision or independently verified internal command-safeguard record was recovered.

## 2B — Peace, security, and violence

**E037 — 2B.1, 2B.3, 2B.7, 2B.10**

Turkey’s official account of the 29 March 2022 Istanbul meeting records that Russian and Ukrainian delegations met for negotiations after the invasion. This confirms a diplomatic channel and a possible alternative to continued war, but does not establish Putin’s personal negotiating instructions or why the process failed.

Locator: Turkish Directorate of Communications, 29 March 2022, report on the Istanbul delegation meeting.  
Source: [Turkish government meeting record](https://www.iletisim.gov.tr/english/haberler/detay/meeting-of-russia-ukraine-negotiation-delegations-in-istanbul-ends).  
Period fit: direct 2022 event.  
Disposition: final evidence, medium-high; formal diplomatic record, limited causal attribution.

**E038 — 2B.4, 2B.5, 2B.9**

A UN Security Council briefing in September 2022 reported allegations and documentation concerning filtration, arbitrary detention, torture, ill-treatment, and enforced disappearance in Russian-controlled areas. The record explicitly called for unrestricted ICRC and OHCHR access. It supports state-authority and accountability concerns while preserving the distinction between reported violations and adjudicated findings.

Locator: Security Council meeting coverage, 7 September 2022, paragraphs concerning filtration and detention.  
Source: [UN Security Council coverage](https://press.un.org/en/2022/sc15023.doc.htm).  
Period fit: direct 2022 reporting.  
Disposition: final evidence, high authority; attribution strongest for Russian-controlled authorities, not every individual act.

**E039 — 2B.5, 2B.9, 2B.10**

The ICRC’s 2022 statement records that it had visited hundreds, but not all, POWs and had been denied access to all POW locations, including Olenivka. This is an access and accountability failure, not evidence that every detainee was mistreated.

Locator: ICRC statement, October 2022, paragraphs on visits and denied access.  
Source: [ICRC access statement](https://www.icrc.org/en/document/ukraine-russia-icrc-asks-immediate-and-unimpeded-access-to-all-prisoners-of-war).  
Period fit: direct 2022 statement.  
Disposition: final evidence, high authority; access-gap evidence.

Contrary evidence was attempted through OHCHR material documenting alleged mistreatment by Ukrainian forces as well as Russian forces. This does not neutralize the Russian evidence but prevents a one-sided attribution record.

## 3B — Rights and physical security

No fully new, nationally attributable corrective or remedy record was recovered. The strongest continuation result was the UN Security Council detention record above, which is foreign-conflict evidence and should not be duplicated as domestic-rights evidence.

Shortfall remains in:

- domestic prison and torture monitoring;
- effective remedies and corrective action;
- minority and vulnerable-group outcomes;
- non-state violence tolerated or remedied by the state.

Existing E025, E028, and E029 remain usable with their prior attribution limits.

## 4B — Institutions, law, and information

**E040 — 4B.3, 4B.6, 4B.9, 4B.10**

Freedom House records that Russian authorities blocked Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram in 2022, designated Meta an extremist organization, and issued March orders affecting state-media hosting and DNS infrastructure. These are attributable state institutional actions; Putin’s formal authority supports responsibility for the national policy environment, but not necessarily each technical implementation decision.

Locator: Freedom on the Net 2022, Russia, paragraphs 146–153.  
Source: [Freedom House](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-net/2022).  
Period fit: direct 2022 country report.  
Disposition: final evidence, medium-high.

**E041 — 4B.3, 4B.6, 4B.9**

Amnesty records the 24 February Roskomnadzor order requiring media to rely only on official sources and avoid terms such as “war” and “invasion,” followed by blocking of independent outlets and the departure of at least 150 journalists.

Locator: Amnesty report, paragraphs 67–78.  
Source: [Amnesty International](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2022/03/russia-kremlins-ruthless-crackdown-stifles-independent-journalism-and-anti-war-movement/).  
Period fit: direct 2022 events.  
Disposition: final evidence, medium-high; attribution to Roskomnadzor and national policy, not necessarily personal drafting by Putin.

Election-transfer evidence remains structurally limited because 2022 was not a federal presidential election year. Regional election, judicial-remedy, and independent internet-measurement coverage remains incomplete.

## 5B — Economic governance

**E042 — 5B.2, 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.9**

Rosstat’s 2022 poverty materials provide an official household-level source family for the poverty threshold and the population below it. The material is useful for distributional exposure, but the accessible search record did not provide a sufficiently precise extract of the final national rate to support a numerical claim here.

Locator: Rosstat 2022 poverty-boundary and revised poverty-population releases.  
Sources: [Rosstat revised 2022 poverty data](https://www.rosstat.gov.ru/folder/313/document/205321), [Rosstat Q4 2022 poverty boundary](https://rosstat.gov.ru/folder/313/document/200416).  
Period fit: direct 2022 statistical releases.  
Disposition: discovery/final-candidate evidence; numerical extraction requires local verification.

**E043 — 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.9; cross-link 6B.6, 6B.9, 8B.6**

The Russian Social Fund’s reported execution of the 2022 Pension and Social Insurance budgets states that pension-fund income was 12.5 trillion rubles, expenditure 11.4 trillion, 9.6 trillion went to pensions, and 1 trillion supported families with children. It also reports two pension indexations and states that obligations were fulfilled on time.

Locator: Social Fund report, 11 July 2023, paragraphs 238–249.  
Source: [Social Fund budget-execution report](https://sfr.gov.ru/press_center/news/~2023/07/11/252057).  
Period fit: retrospective official report on 2022 execution.  
Disposition: final formal-record evidence, medium; favorable official claim requiring independent distributional verification.

Contrary search located no independent 2022 household-level assessment sufficient to verify whether these transfers offset inflation and sanctions exposure across regions. The chapter remains short of evidence on capture, appointments, budget leakage, and realized household welfare.

## 6B — Social governance

E044 — 6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.6, 6B.9

The Social Fund’s 2022 execution report provides a concrete delivery record for pensions, disability and veteran payments, maternity-related benefits, and family support. It is useful evidence of formal program execution, but it does not establish service quality, access equality, poverty reduction, or Putin-specific operational management.

Locator: Social Fund report, paragraphs 241–249.  
Source: [Social Fund report](https://sfr.gov.ru/press_center/news/~2023/07/11/252057).  
Period fit: direct retrospective 2022 execution.  
Disposition: final formal-record evidence, medium; official self-report.

Shortfall remains substantial for:

- housing and sanitation;
- regional service variation;
- vulnerable-group outcomes;
- health and education implementation;
- independent verification of social-protection delivery.

## 7B — Integrity and corruption

No new source recovered during this pass met the threshold for a new Putin-specific personal-integrity unit.

The contrary search located official disclosure infrastructure and presidential asset-information pages, but not a sufficiently precise 2022 declaration extract that could be safely added as a factual unit. Existing E030 and E031 remain usable only with their stated limits: documentary network tracing and a U.S. sanctions finding do not prove personal ownership, criminal liability, or personal benefit.

The chapter remains high-risk and short of:

- independently verified beneficial ownership;
- appointment/conflict-of-interest records;
- direct deception or disclosure evidence;
- audits, corrections, or integrity investigations.

## 8B — Governing effectiveness

**E045 — 8B.2, 8B.6, 8B.9**

The Social Fund’s execution figures provide a formal implementation record for pensions, family benefits, disability and veteran payments during 2022. This is a concrete program-output unit and favorable/mitigating evidence, but it does not establish portfolio-wide effectiveness or durable outcomes.

Locator: Social Fund report, paragraphs 241–249.  
Source: [Social Fund report](https://sfr.gov.ru/press_center/news/~2023/07/11/252057).  
Period fit: retrospective 2022 execution.  
Disposition: final formal-record evidence, medium; not independent outcome evaluation.

**E046 — 8B.1, 8B.2, 8B.6**

The Russian government’s budget documentation supplies a formal record of budget and program planning for the 2023–25 period, relevant to the existence of a governing portfolio after the 2022 shock. It does not demonstrate execution, adaptation, durability, or outcomes during 2022.

Locator: Russian government budget-document archive.  
Source: [Russian government budget documentation](https://government.ru/docs/all/144850/).  
Period fit: linked planning and formal-record context; limited direct 2022 fit.  
Disposition: context/formal-record evidence, medium-low.

A targeted contrary search for independent implementation audits found references to Accounts Chamber and pension-budget execution materials, but no accessible audit extract that could safely establish a 2022 program failure or success attributable to Putin. Chapter 8B therefore remains incomplete at the portfolio and outcome levels.

## Global disposition

The continuation recovered:

- one new arms-control compliance/restraint unit;
- one institutional arms-control implementation unit;
- one Turkish diplomatic-process unit;
- two detention/access units;
- two internet-control units;
- one household-statistics candidate;
- two social-transfer/execution units;
- one formal budget-record unit.

The main gaps remain research-recoverable but unresolved: primary nuclear doctrine and safeguards, negotiation decision ownership, domestic remedies, household distribution, independent social-service outcomes, verified personal benefit, and audited governing-program effectiveness.
